title: The lead pipeline board
summary: See every open lead as a card on its stage, move leads along by dragging, and focus the board on what needs you.

body.text: The **Leads** page is a board. Each column is a stage in your sales process, and each card is a lead — a customer you're trying to sell to. The top of the page shows how many leads are open and their total value.
Reading a card
Cards start folded: the customer's name, the product and a few icons. Press the **⌄** arrow on a card to see the rest.

items: The **customer's name**, the product and colour, and the lead's title.
The **value**, with a **×N** badge when they want more than one.
Who the lead is **assigned to**.
The **next step** — the next planned call, meeting or follow-up — and a test-drive booking if there is one.

body.text: Moving a lead

items: Drag a card into another column.
Let go. The move saves straight away, and anything set to happen at that stage runs.
Dragging into the test-drive stage opens a booking window — see **Booking a test drive from the board**.

body.text: A stage can require something before a lead enters it — for example a reason or a date. If so, a window asks for it first.
Moving a lead back before the test-drive stage cancels a test drive already booked for it, so an old appointment never hangs around.
Focusing the board

items: **Search** narrows the cards by customer, product, source or next step.
**All owners** lets you pick one salesperson's leads.
**Needs attention** shows only leads with no next step, an overdue step, or seven or more days in the same stage.
**Clear** resets everything.

body.text: **Won / Lost** lists closed deals, and **List view** shows leads as a table you can filter. **New lead** adds one.

Moving a lead needs the **Move leads between stages in the same pipeline** permission, and moving it to another pipeline needs **Move leads to a different sales pipeline**. Without them the move is refused.

title: Creating a new lead
summary: Log a new sales opportunity — only the customer's name is required.

body.text: Press **New lead** on the Leads page (or use **Ctrl+K → New lead** anywhere). Only the customer's name is required; the rest makes follow-up and forecasting better.

items: Enter the customer's **name**, and their email and phone number if you have them.
Choose the **product** and **colour**, the **quantity**, and an estimated **value**.
Choose the **stage**, or leave it blank to start at the first stage of your default pipeline.
Choose who it's **assigned to**, the **source** (where the customer came from) and any notes.
Save.

body.text: Every lead belongs to a customer. If you don't pick one, the CRM links an existing customer with the same email or phone number, or creates a new customer from the lead's details — so you don't end up with duplicates.
You need the **Create leads** permission. To assign a lead to someone else you also need **Assign leads to users and teams**; without it, the lead is assigned to you.
A lead can't be created straight into a won or lost stage. Create it, then use **Mark won** or **Mark lost**.
Leads also arrive by themselves from your website, Facebook and Instagram lead ads, WhatsApp and the chatbot — you don't need to type those in.

title: Working a lead through to close
summary: Everything on a lead's page: quotes, won and lost, the tabs, and the full history.

body.text: Click a lead to open its page. The top shows its stage (or won/lost), value, product, and how many activities and quotes it has.
What you can do on an open lead

items: **Create quote** — starts a quote for this customer with the lead's product already on it.

**Mark won** — closes the deal as won. Pick the quote the customer accepted: it's accepted exactly as if you'd pressed **Accepted** on it, and the deal moves on to Deliveries. If there was no quote, choose to mark it won without one.
**Mark lost** — closes it as lost, with a reason, so you can see later why deals were lost.

body.text: A closed lead shows **Reopen** instead, which makes it open again and clears the lost reason. After a win, a banner offers to **register the vehicle**, so its servicing can be tracked.
The tabs

rows: The lead's details, to read and edit. For leads that came from your website or an ad, you can also see exactly what the customer submitted.
The customer this lead belongs to — link a different one if needed
Calls, meetings and follow-ups for this lead — plan them and mark them done

body.text: The timeline on the right brings together every change, message and activity, so the whole story of the deal is in one place.
**Mark won**, **Mark lost** and **Reopen** each need their own permission (**Mark leads won**, **Mark leads lost**, **Reopen won or lost leads**). If a button is missing, ask an owner.

title: Booking a test drive from the board
summary: Moving a lead into the test-drive stage books the drive at the same time.

body.text: When a lead moves into the test-drive stage, you're asked to book the drive there and then, so it's never forgotten.

items: Drag the lead into the test-drive column.
Choose the **model to drive**, or keep the one they're interested in.
Set the **date**, **time** and **location** — your showroom is filled in for you.
Press **Book & move**.

body.text: The drive is saved as a planned test-drive activity on the lead and shown on the calendar. The card then shows the appointment and, when available, that day's weather forecast.
Need the customer to sign an indemnity before the drive? Use **Indemnity** on the lead's page.

title: The lead list and saved views
summary: See leads as a table, filter them any way you like, and save the filters you use often.

body.text: **List view** on the Leads page shows the leads you can see as a table — handy when you want to sort by value, age or where leads came from.
Filtering

items: **Status** — open, won or lost.
**Source** — Facebook, Instagram, website, WhatsApp, referral, manual or walk-in.
**Pipeline** and **Stage**.
**Value at least** and **Created in last N days**.

body.text: Saving a view

items: Set the filters you want.
Type a name under **Name this view** and press **Save view**.
The view appears as a button — click it to come back to it, or **×** to delete it.

body.text: Won and lost deals
**Won / Lost** lists closed deals with the date they closed and, for lost ones, the reason. With the **Reopen won or lost leads** permission, each row has **Reopen** to bring the deal back.

title: Browsing and adding customers
summary: Find customers and companies, and add new ones.

body.text: **Contacts** is your list of customers and companies. The strip at the top shows how many are listed, how many vehicles they own, and how many open deals they have.
Finding someone

items: **Search** by name, company, email or phone number.
Switch between **Cards** and **List**.
Each card shows tags, vehicles and open deals, their main contact detail and who looks after them.

body.text: Arranging the list

items: In **List**, click a column heading to sort by it; click again to reverse. The order applies to every page, not just the one you are on, and a link you share keeps it.

Press **Columns** to show or hide columns (Owner and City are hidden to start with), move them up or down, set a width in pixels, and choose **Comfortable** or **Compact** rows. Press **Save layout** — it is yours alone, kept for this workspace, and **Reset** puts the standard layout back.
Tick contacts to select them. Ticking the box in the heading selects this page only; to take every matching contact across all pages, press **Select all** — it is never done for you.
**Preview** checks every selected contact against what you are allowed to see right now and tells you how many are included and how many were left out. There are no bulk changes for contacts yet.
On a phone the list shows as cards with the most useful details, rather than a wide table.

body.text: Adding a customer

items: Press **New contact**.
Enter at least a first name; add company, email, phone, WhatsApp and address as needed.
Tick **Is company** for a business. Set where they came from and who looks after them, and add **tags** separated by commas — each tag gets its own colour.
Save.

body.text: You see the customers your permissions allow — every customer, or only the ones linked to your work. Adding customers needs **Create contacts**; the **Duplicates** tool needs **Merge duplicate contacts**.

title: Inside a customer profile
summary: Everything about one customer: details, activities, vehicles, deals, referrals and privacy requests.

body.text: Open a customer to see everything about them. The top shows their health — how the relationship is going — and counts of their vehicles, open deals, planned activities and documents.
The tabs

rows: Contact details, address, where they came from, and notes
Their vehicles with service-due badges — and add a vehicle
Every deal, with its value and stage

body.text: Referrals

Each customer has their own referral code, which you can copy or send by WhatsApp. New leads that come in with the code are listed here. When a referred deal is won, the reward becomes **due**; press **Redeem** and note what was given.
Privacy requests (POPIA)

items: Record **consent** as given or withdrawn, and where it came from.
**Export data** downloads everything held about the customer.
**Right to erasure** removes their personal details everywhere and moves the customer to Trash.

body.text: Erasure is for owners only and can't be undone — use it only for a genuine erasure request. Vehicles, job cards and safety records are kept without their personal details, for warranty and legal reasons.
**Edit** changes their details. **Delete** moves the customer to Trash for 60 days. A customer with a sale or signed paperwork can't be deleted, so their documents stay complete.

title: Finding and merging duplicate contacts
summary: Combine customers that were entered twice, keeping all their history on one record.

body.text: The **Duplicates** page groups customers that share an email address or phone number, so you can combine them into one.

items: Look through each group. The shared email or phone is shown, with each record's deals, vehicles and messages to help you choose which to keep.
On the record to keep, press **Keep this one → merge others in**.
Type a short reason and confirm.

body.text: Everything linked to the others — deals, vehicles, job cards, quotes, messages, activities, documents and history — moves onto the one you kept, and their tags are added. Empty fields on the kept record are filled from the others. The merged-away records go to Trash.
A merge can't be undone. Check you're keeping the right record first. You need the **Merge duplicate contacts** permission and access to every customer in the group.

title: Working your activity queue
summary: Your list of planned calls, meetings and follow-ups — and how to complete or cancel them.

body.text: **Activities** lists the follow-ups planned for you and your team. The cards at the top count how many are planned, overdue, due today and coming up.
Choosing what you see

items: **Mine** shows only yours; **Accessible** shows everything you're allowed to see.
**Search** by the activity, the customer, the lead or who it's for. Filter by **type**: call, email, WhatsApp, meeting, test drive or to-do.
Activities are grouped by when they're due, overdue first.

body.text: Completing an activity

items: Optionally type what happened in the activity's **outcome note**.
Press **Done**. The note is added to the customer's history.
If it was the lead's last planned step, you're asked to plan the next one, so no lead goes quiet.

body.text: Use the bin icon to **cancel** an activity you no longer need.
Seeing activities needs **View activities and calendars**; adding, completing and cancelling them needs **Create, assign and complete activities**.

title: The sales calendar
summary: Your team's meetings, calls and test drives on a calendar.

body.text: The **Calendar** shows activities on a calendar in your workspace's time zone. Both planned and completed ones are shown, so past appointments stay visible; only cancelled ones are hidden.

items: Move between periods with the calendar's controls, and filter by person with **All owners**.
Sales activities are shown here; workshop bookings are on the workshop calendar.
If you can manage activities, you can add and change them right on the calendar.

body.text: Adding an activity

items: Give it a **summary** and choose a **type**.
Set the **due date** and time, a **location**, and who it's **assigned to**.
Optionally link it to a lead or customer, then save.

body.text: Turn on **Meeting reminders** under Notifications to be alerted an hour before a timed meeting or test drive — tapping the alert opens the location in Google Maps.

title: Managing fleets
summary: Group vehicles and customers under one account — an estate, golf course, lodge, resort or business.

body.text: **Fleets** groups vehicles and people under one account — for example an estate, golf course, lodge, resort or business — so you can see the whole account's service and warranty status at a glance.
Creating a fleet

items: Under **Create a fleet**, enter the fleet's name.
Choose the **Account type** and, optionally, the main contact.
Press **Create fleet**.

body.text: Inside a fleet

items: Counts of its **Vehicles**, how many are **Due for service** and how many are **In warranty**.
A list of its vehicles, each with a service badge and a warranty badge. Add a vehicle from the unassigned ones, or remove one.
**Fleet details** — the main contact is the fleet manager, the one person you phone.
**Business details** — registration and VAT numbers, billing email and phone, and address, then **Save business details**.
The people linked to the fleet, and their deals and job cards.

body.text: Deleting a fleet keeps its vehicles — they simply become unassigned.

title: Reading customer health
summary: One score per customer, so you know who to look after and who to win back.

body.text: **Customer health** combines what they own, how recently they've been serviced, their feedback, referrals and any open problems into one score, so you know who's happy and who might be drifting away.

rows: Worth some attention before things slip
Reach out and try to win them back

body.text: The top row counts customers in each tier. Below are your top **VIP customers** and the customers most **at risk**, each with the reasons behind their score. Click a name to open their profile.
Scores update by themselves as things change — there's nothing to recalculate. The same health badge is shown at the top of every customer's profile.

title: Search and the command menu
summary: Find any customer, deal, quote, vehicle or document, and jump anywhere with the keyboard.

body.text: **Search** looks through the customers, leads, quotes, vehicles, job cards, customer cases, documents and products you're allowed to see, grouped by type.

items: Search by name, company, email, phone, city, model, VIN or registration.
Type a number to find a quote (Q-…), a case (C-…) or a job card.
You only ever see results you have access to.

body.text: The command menu
Press **Ctrl+K** (**⌘K** on a Mac) anywhere to open it.

items: **Quick actions** — new lead, new contact, new job card, and search.
**Go to** — jump to any page.
**Settings** — open any part of Settings directly.

body.text: The menu only shows what you're allowed to do, so it's a quick way to whatever you use most.
